questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay related to the short passage given below. In your essay, you are to comment on the phenomenon described in the passage and suggest measures to address the issue. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. Nowadays star chasing is prevalent among many teenagers. They take pop stars as their idols, imitating their way of talking, following their style of dressing9 and seeking every chance to meet them in person at great expenses.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
The passage vividly presents a common scene: many teenagers today are obsessed with pop stars, copying how their idols talk and dress and spending heavily just to see them face to face. In my view, this phenomenon deserves a balanced judgement rather than blind praise or total denial.

Admittedly, taking an admirable star as one's idol can be positively motivating, since a hard-working singer may inspire young people to pursue their own dreams. However, when admiration turns into blind worship, the harm outweighs the benefit. Chasing stars at great expense drains teenagers' limited money and time, distracts them from their studies, and may even distort their values.

To address the issue, joint efforts are needed. Parents and schools should guide adolescents to build a rational view of idols, while the media ought to promote genuine role models instead of empty fame. For teenagers themselves, the key is to learn from a star's strengths without losing themselves. Only in this way can idol worship become a source of growth rather than regret.

transcript.text: M: Good morning and welcome to People in the News. With me today is Meghan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book Beyond Recycling is making headlines.
transcript.zh: M: 早上好，欢迎收看《新闻人物》。今天和我一起做节目的是 Meghan Brown，一位环保活动人士。她那本颇具争议的新书《Beyond Recycling》正在成为新闻焦点。

transcript.text: W: Hi, Brian. Thanks for having me today. I'm excited to explain to the audience what my book is really about.
transcript.zh: W: 你好，Brian。谢谢你今天邀请我来。我很高兴能向观众解释我的书到底讲的是什么。

transcript.text: M: Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country. Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal.
transcript.zh: M: 批评你这本书的人声称，你试图迫使整个国家发生激进的改变。有人说，你想强迫所有人都吃素，并让私人交通工具变得非法。

transcript.text: W: I'm aware of those claims, but they simply aren't true. People who haven't read the book are making assumptions about my arguments. They know I'm a vegetarian, that I don't wear leather or fur, and that I always use public transportation. So they're depicting me as a radical animal rights activist and environmentalist determined to force my beliefs on others.
transcript.zh: W: 我知道这些说法，但它们根本不是真的。那些没读过这本书的人在擅自揣测我的观点。他们知道我是素食主义者，不穿皮革或皮草，而且总是乘坐公共交通。所以，他们把我描述成一个激进的动物权利活动人士和环保主义者，认定我决心把自己的信仰强加给别人。

transcript.text: M: But don't you want others to adopt your practices? You've campaigned for animal rights and the environment for decades.
transcript.zh: M: 但你难道不希望别人也采取你的生活方式吗？你为动物权利和环境问题奔走了几十年。

transcript.text: W: I'd love it if people choose to live as I do. But my life choices are based on my personal convictions. They aren't my recommendations for others who don't share those convictions.
transcript.zh: W: 如果人们选择像我这样生活，我当然会很高兴。但我的生活选择是基于我个人的信念。对于那些不认同这些信念的人来说，这并不是我的建议。

transcript.text: M: Well, in this excerpt from your book, you argue that meat consumption and private transport are devastating the environment and that the best choices for the planet are vegetarian diets and public transport.
transcript.zh: M: 那么，在你书中的这段节选里，你认为食用肉类和使用私人交通工具正在严重破坏环境，而对地球来说，最好的选择是素食和公共交通。

transcript.text: W: I did write that. But those are examples of what I call best practices, not what I'm actually suggesting. In my guidelines for saving the environment, I suggest modest changes, like eating vegetarian meals two days a week.
transcript.zh: W: 我的确写了这些。但那只是我所说的最佳做法的例子，并不是我实际提出的建议。在我关于保护环境的指导中，我建议进行一些适度的改变，比如每周吃两天素食。

transcript.text: M: You also endorse high taxes on meat and other animal products and increased taxes on gasoline. Those taxes could force poor people to adopt your life choices.
transcript.zh: M: 你还支持对肉类和其他动物制品征收高额税，并提高汽油税。这些税收可能会迫使穷人采用你的生活方式。

transcript.text: W: But the taxes I suggest aren't that high, less than 3% only. Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection, which benefits everyone.
transcript.zh: W: 但我建议的税率并不高，只有不到3%。此外，筹集到的钱将用于环境保护，而这会让每个人都受益。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman's new book?

options.text: It has given rise to much controversy.
It has been very favorably received.
It was primarily written for vegetarians.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：With me today is Meghan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book Beyond Recycling is making headlines.信号：开场介绍即定性句 。主持人开场介绍嘉宾时用 controversial new book 直接给书定了性，开场点题句往往就是答案句，不必等转折。

optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：It has been very favorably received. 说广受好评，与原文 controversial(有争议)方向相反；有争议恰恰意味着评价两极，不等于一致叫好。 借用原文：They know I'm a vegetarian
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：It was primarily written for vegetarians. 借了后文反复出现的素食话题，但录音从未说这本书「主要写给素食者」；vegetarian 是真听到的词，可这句话原文没说，是典型听到原词就想选。 借用原文：as a radical animal rights activist and environmentalist
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：It offends many environmentalists. 用了 environmentalist 这个反复出现的词，但原文说她被人「描绘成」环保活动家，从没说这本书「冒犯了许多环保人士」，属凭原词臆造。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（controversial new book ↔ It has given rise to much controversy. 形容词转名词化）

questions.evidenceText: With me today is Meghan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book Beyond Recycling is making headlines.

questions.stem: What do some critics say about the author of the book?

options.text: She neglects people's efforts in animal protection.
She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas.
She ignores the various benefits of public transport.
She insists vegetarians are harming the environment.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P3）：Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country. Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal.信号：Critics assert 转述信号 。出现 Critics of your book assert that 这一转述信号，明确告诉你下面就是批评者的说法，正对题干的 critics，是答案句标志。

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：She neglects people's efforts in animal protection. 提到 animal protection 蹭了动物话题，但批评者从没说她「忽视他人的动保努力」，原文无此评价。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：She ignores the various benefits of public transport. 用了反复出现的 public transport，但批评者根本没说她「无视公共交通的好处」——恰恰相反，她是支持公共交通的，这是把话题词乱拼成的指控。 借用原文：you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：She insists vegetarians are harming the environment. 用了 vegetarian 和 environment 两个高频词，但批评者说的是她想强迫大家吃素，绝非说「素食者在破坏环境」，意思被拧反了。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country ↔ She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas. 几近同词的核心保留）

questions.evidenceText: Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country. Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal.

questions.stem: What does the woman claim about the diet changes she suggested?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P8）：In my guidelines for saving the environment, I suggest modest changes, like eating vegetarian meals two days a week.信号：I suggest+定性词 。她亲口说 I suggest modest changes，suggest 后紧跟的形容词就是她对所建议改变的定性，是这题答案信号。

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：They are significant. 说重大，与她自述的 modest(温和)程度相反；她特意强调改变不大，significant 正好拧反。 借用原文：force radical changes
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：They are revolutionary. 革命性，呼应了前文批评者说的 radical，但那是批评者的指控，她本人恰恰否认并改称 modest，把批评口吻当成她的定性就上当了。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：They are rational. 理性的，听起来像褒义合理，但录音里她用的词是 modest 而非 rational，原文从未称这些改变「理性」。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I suggest modest changes ↔ They are modest. 同词直接还原）

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her suggested tax increase?

options.text: It would help to protect the environment.
It would generate money for public health.
It would need support from the general public.
It would force poor people to change their diet.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P10）：But the taxes I suggest aren't that high, less than 3% only. Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection, which benefits everyone.信号：Plus 之后补出关键好处 。她先用 But 澄清税不高，再用 Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection 补出加…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：It would generate money for public health. 借了原文 the money generated，但钱的去向是 environmental protection(环保)而非 public health(公共卫生)，把用途偷换了。 借用原文：Those taxes could force poor people to adopt your life choices.
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：It would need support from the general public. 听着合理，但她谈加税时只说税率低、钱用于环保，从没说这措施「需要公众支持」，是无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：It would force poor people to change their diet. 含 force 和 poor people，但这是主持人质疑时的说法(第9段)，正是她要反驳的，不是她自己对加税的说法，题干问的是她怎么说。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection ↔ It would help to protect the environment. 措施钱去向=保护环境）

transcript.text: M: With me in the studio today is Ms. Jane Logan, author of a new book, Secrets to Success. She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success. So Ms. Logan, in your book, you claim that successful people have many things in common. For instance, they know their strengths when pursuing a goal.
transcript.zh: M: 今天和我一起在演播室的是简·洛根女士，她是新书《成功的秘诀》的作者。她声称自己已经揭示了人们取得成功的方式。那么，洛根女士，在您的书中，您声称成功人士有许多共同之处。比如说，他们在追求目标时清楚自己的优势。

transcript.text: W: That's right. They also tend to be motivated by a negative or positive life event. They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。他们往往还会受到人生中某个积极或消极事件的激励。他们把自己的成功归功于生命中有一个相信他们的人。

transcript.text: M: You also write that there are a number of different factors related to success. And while successful people are driven to achieve their goals, the ultra successful have even greater ambition.
transcript.zh: M: 您还写道，成功与许多不同因素有关。成功人士会努力实现自己的目标，而那些极其成功的人则有更大的抱负。

transcript.text: W: Yes, greater ambition as well as a burning desire to be the best of the best is also a common characteristic.
transcript.zh: W: 是的，更大的抱负，以及成为最优秀中的最优秀者的强烈愿望，也是一个共同特征。

transcript.text: M: Right. So those who are determined don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome.
transcript.zh: M: 没错。所以，那些意志坚定的人不会把障碍看成阻止成功的东西，而只会把它们视为需要克服的不便。

transcript.text: W: Absolutely. Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals.
transcript.zh: W: 当然。成功人士也很乐观，因为在意识到可能阻碍我们实现目标的障碍的同时，保持积极的心态非常重要。

transcript.text: M: That's a good point. All too often, people give up at the first hurdle. Would you say then that most successful people make it all by themselves?
transcript.zh: M: 说得好。人们往往在遇到第一个障碍时就放弃了。那么，您是否认为大多数成功人士都是完全靠自己取得成功的呢？

transcript.text: W: Not exactly. They are usually good at cooperating with people and understanding the needs of others.
transcript.zh: W: 不完全是。他们通常很善于与人合作，也善于理解他人的需求。

transcript.text: M: So people will be willing to help them, I guess.
transcript.zh: M: 所以我想，人们会愿意帮助他们。

transcript.text: W: That's correct. And this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect, whether it's with a colleague, an assistant or even a receptionist.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。而且，这往往会带来极大的相互尊重，无论对方是同事、助理，还是前台接待员。

transcript.text: M: Most successful people I know are very passionate about their work. Would you say that passion is the single biggest key to success?
transcript.zh: M: 我认识的大多数成功人士都对自己的工作充满热情。您认为热情是成功的最大关键吗？

transcript.text: W: Not entirely. There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion. If that exists, success will follow.
transcript.zh: W: 不完全是。有一个前提条件，也就是说，你必须在一个能够培养热情的环境中工作。如果这一点具备了，成功就会随之而来。

questions.stem: What has the woman revealed in her book?

options.text: Where successful people's strengths come from.
Why many people fight so hard for success.
How she achieved her life's goal.

questions.analysis: 主旨题。答案句（P1）：She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success.信号：开头点题句 。主持人开场介绍时一句 She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success. 直接交代了全书主题，开头点题正是主旨题的核心定位信号。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音确说成功者 they know their strengths when pursuing a goal，A 把 strengths 单拎出来问 "strengths 从哪来"，但 "strengths 的来源" 录音根本没讲，且它只是众多特征之一，不是全书主旨。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 问 "为什么很多人拼命追求成功"（原因），但全篇谈的是成功者 "有哪些共同特征"，从未讨论 "人为何要拼命求成功" 这个动机问题，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：C 说 "她（作者）如何实现人生目标"，但录音里这位女士是在 "揭示别人成功的规律"，谈的是 people / successful people，不是讲她自己的成功经历，主语张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（how people achieve success ↔ What makes people successful. "如何获得成功"="什么造就成功"）

questions.evidenceText: She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success.

questions.stem: What do successful people attribute their achievements to?

options.text: Having someone who has confidence in them.
Having someone who is ready to help them.
Having a firm belief in their own ability.
Having a realistic attitude towards life.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them.信号：归因信号 credit...to 。被问者（女士）的应答 They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them.…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B "有人随时愿帮他们" 与 A 仅差核心词。录音说的是 someone who believes in them（相信），不是 "愿意帮忙"。"愿帮忙" 是后文 people will be willing to help them 才提到、且属另一道题的内容，搬到这里就答非所问。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：C "对自身能力有坚定信念" 把主语换成了 "自己"，而录音明确是 someone...who believes in them——是 "别人相信他"，主语方向相反。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D "对生活持现实态度" 在整段归因表述里完全没出现，录音只说归功于 "有人相信他们"，与 "现实态度" 无关，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（someone in their life who believes in them ↔ Having someone who has confidence in them. believes in=has confidence in）

questions.evidenceText: They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them.

questions.stem: What do successful people do when faced with difficulties?

options.text: They try hard to appear optimistic.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals.信号：困难词 obstacles 附近的描述 。被问者说 it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles，obstacles（障碍）这一困难词…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：A "相应调整目标"，但录音第 5 段说成功者 don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome——是 "克服障碍" 而非 "改目标"，方向相反。 借用原文：Successful people are also optimistic
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：B "努力让自己显得乐观"，录音确说 optimistic、stay positive，但那是 "真的保持积极"，不是 "appear（装作）乐观"，selflessly 加了一个 "装样子" 的意思，曲解原意。
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：D "remain calm（保持冷静）" 与 C "stay positive（保持积极）" 极易混，但录音说的是 positive / optimistic（积极乐观），从未说 calm（冷静），用近义词偷梁换柱。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（stay positive ↔ They stay positive. 原话直接对应）

questions.evidenceText: Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals.

questions.stem: What is one prerequisite for passion at work according to the woman?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P12）：There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion.信号：明示信号 prerequisite + have to 。被问者直接说 There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A "an understanding leadership"，前提句只讲 "培育激情的环境"，全程未提 "领导"；understanding 一词倒是在别处 understanding the needs of others 出现过、但那是讲 "理解他人需求" 的合作，与领导无关。 借用原文：this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C "同事间相互尊重"，mutual respect 确在录音 this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect 出现过，但那是讲合作 "带来" 的结果、且属第 6-7 题语境，不是 "激情的前提"，搬来此处答非所问。 借用原文：good at cooperating with people
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：D "highly cooperative teammates"，录音确说成功者 good at cooperating with people，但那是讲成功者自身的合作能力，不是 "激情的前提"；把合作内容嫁接到前提题上属张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（an environment that nurtures passion ↔ A nurturing environment. 动词短语压缩成名词短语）

questions.evidenceText: There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion.

transcript.text: The saying "blind as a bat" simply isn't correct. The truth is that all 1100 bat species can see and often their vision is pretty good, although not as excellent as other night-hunting animals.
transcript.zh: “像蝙蝠一样瞎”这种俗语根本不正确。事实是，所有1100种蝙蝠都有视力，而且它们的视力通常相当不错，尽管不如其他夜间捕猎的动物那样出色。

transcript.text: There are two main groups of bats, which are believed to have evolved independently of each other, but both from a common ancestor. The first group, known as the mega bats, are mostly medium-sized or large bats who eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish. These species have distinctive visual centers and big eyes. They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey. For example, Flying Foxes not only see well during daylight, but can also distinguish colors. They actually rely on their daylight vision and cannot fly during the night with no moonlight.
transcript.zh: 蝙蝠主要分为两大类，据信它们是从共同祖先独立演化而来的。第一类被称为大蝙蝠，大多是中型或大型蝙蝠，以水果、花朵为食，有时也吃小动物或鱼类。这些物种拥有独特的视觉中心和大眼睛。它们利用视觉和嗅觉来捕获猎物。例如，狐蝠不仅在白天视力良好，还能分辨颜色。它们实际上依赖白天的视力，在没有月光的夜晚无法飞行。

transcript.text: The second group, called micro bats, are smaller in size and mostly eat insects. These species use echolocation to find their way and identify food. Scientists have proven that despite their poorly developed small eyes, these bats still can see during the day. When we consider the nightly lifestyle of these bats, we will see they have to be sensitive to the changing light levels because this is how they sense when to start hunting. Moreover, vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances, beyond the range of echolocation.

transcript.text: A study has found that educational TV shows come with an added lesson that influences the child's behavior. Children who spend more time watching educational programs increase their emotional aggression toward other children. This shows that children can learn the educational lesson that was intended. However, they're also learning other things along the way.
transcript.zh: 一项研究发现，教育类电视节目还附带着一堂会影响儿童行为的课程。花更多时间观看教育类节目的儿童，会增加对其他儿童的情绪性攻击行为。这表明，儿童能够学会节目原本 intended 的教育内容。然而，在此过程中，他们也会学到其他东西。

transcript.text: This unintended impact has to do with the portrayal of conflict in media and how preschool-age children comprehend that conflict. TV and movie producers often incorporate an element of bad behavior. This is to teach children a lesson at the end of the program. Educational shows have pro-education and pro-social goals. However, conflict between characters is often depicted with characters being unkind to each other or they may use emotionally aggressive tactics with each other. Preschool children really don't get the moral of the story. That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together. You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills to be able to do that. These are still developing in young children.
transcript.zh: 这种非预期影响与媒体对冲突的呈现方式以及学龄前儿童对冲突的理解方式有关。电视和电影制作者经常加入不良行为元素，以便在节目结尾教给儿童一个道理。教育类节目具有促进教育和促进社会性发展的目标。然而，人物之间的冲突通常被刻画为人物彼此不友善，或者彼此采用情绪性攻击手段。学龄前儿童确实无法理解故事的寓意。这是因为他们需要理解节目中的各个部分是如何相互联系、共同构成整体的。要做到这一点，需要相当复杂的认知能力和记忆能力，而这些能力在幼儿身上仍在发展之中。

transcript.text: However, parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing. Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot. Parents can comment along the way and then explain the message at the end. They should explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate. This will help children interpret and get the message and help them learn to watch the show for those messages.
transcript.zh: 然而，家长不应该完全限制儿童观看电视。相反，家长应该陪孩子一起观看，并帮助他们理解情节。家长可以在观看过程中发表评论，然后在结尾解释其中传达的信息。他们应该说明某些行为方式为什么是不恰当的。这将帮助儿童理解并领会节目传达的信息，也帮助他们学会关注节目中的这些信息。

transcript.text: While it has long been a practice in Asian countries, many people in Western countries have yet to embrace the no-shoes-in-the-house rule. For many in those countries, wiping their shoes before going inside is regarded as sufficient. After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone. But I can give you several good reasons why people should remove their shoes before going inside their homes.
transcript.zh: 虽然在亚洲国家，无鞋入室长期以来一直是一种习惯，但许多西方国家的人仍未接受在屋内不穿鞋的规定。对这些国家的许多人来说，进屋前擦擦鞋就被认为足够了。毕竟，他们可能认为一点灰尘不会伤害任何人。但我可以给你几个人们进屋前应该脱鞋的充分理由。

transcript.text: Bacteria are everywhere. They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets. In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear. They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe. And it only takes a little bit of dirt to damage your timber floors. The more dirt you track in, the more it scratches and the more often you'd have to clean. The extra scrubbing will harm your floors over time. Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels or shoes with pointed or hard parts. These can dent and scratch your floor. And if you live in an apartment building, removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors.
transcript.zh: 细菌无处不在。当你沿着人行道、公共厕所的地面，甚至办公室的地毯行走时，细菌会附着在你的鞋上。在一所美国大学开展的一项研究中，研究人员从鞋子上采集了微小的细菌。他们发现，单只鞋子的外部最多可以聚集421,000个细菌单位。而损坏木地板只需要一点点灰尘。你带进屋里的灰尘越多，地板受到的刮擦就越严重，你需要清洁地板的频率也就越高。额外的擦洗会随着时间的推移损坏地板。鞋子也可能在地板上留下痕迹和划痕，尤其是高跟鞋或带有尖锐、坚硬部件的鞋子。这些鞋子会使地板凹陷并留下划痕。而且，如果你住在公寓楼里，考虑到楼下邻居，脱掉发出声响的鞋子是一种礼貌的做法。

transcript.text: Walking around with bare feet is actually better for your feet. It strengthens the muscles in your feet. Though many people are accustomed to wearing shoes during all their waking hours, the more time you spend wearing shoes, the more likely you are to incur foot injuries as a result.
transcript.zh: 实际上，赤脚走路对你的双脚更有益。它能增强脚部肌肉。尽管许多人已经习惯在清醒的所有时间里都穿鞋，但你穿鞋的时间越长，就越有可能因此受到足部伤害。

transcript.text: And if people aren't yet convinced by my arguments, I can give one final reason. The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home. Toxic chemicals are everywhere in our lives: insect-killing chemicals used on public grass areas, cleaning chemicals on the floors of public areas. By kicking off your shoes before you enter the home, you are denying entry to these harmful chemicals.
transcript.zh: 如果人们还没有被我的论据说服，我还可以给出最后一个理由。你通过鞋子带进屋里的灰尘和有毒化学物质会降低家中的空气质量。有毒化学物质遍布我们的生活：公共草地上使用的杀虫剂，公共场所地面上的清洁剂。进屋前脱掉鞋子，就能阻止这些有害化学物质进入室内。

transcript.text: Given the amount of time we spend in classrooms, and the number of shoes that pass through them every day, you may well understand me if I were to propose a no-shoes-in-the-classroom rule.
transcript.zh: 考虑到我们在教室里度过的时间，以及每天经过教室的鞋子数量，如果我提议制定教室内不穿鞋的规定，你很可能会理解我。

transcript.text: Emotions are an essential and inseparable part of our consciousness. They are part of a built-in mechanism, which allows us to cope with the ups and downs of our lives both physically and mentally. When we hide our emotions and our true feelings, we stop being genuine, spontaneous and authentic in our relationships. When we put on cultivated and polished faces in the company of others, we stop being true to ourselves. Socially, it may be a good tactic to hide our true emotions, but morally it is also a breach of faith and trust. Although humans are more advanced and intelligent, animals are more genuine and authentic in their behavior and responses than human beings. The more educated we are, the less transparent and reliable we become. We are drawn to our pets because pets do not lie.
transcript.zh: 情绪是我们意识中不可或缺且无法分割的一部分。它们是与生俱来的机制的一部分，使我们能够在身心两方面应对生活中的起起落落。当我们隐藏自己的情绪和真实感受时，我们在与他人的关系中便不再真诚、自然和真实。当我们在他人面前摆出经过刻意修饰和精心打磨的面孔时，我们便不再忠于自我。从社会角度看，隐藏真实情绪可能是一种有效的策略，但从道德角度看，这也违背了信任和诚信。尽管人类更加先进、更加聪明，但动物在行为和反应上比人类更加真诚、更加真实。我们受教育程度越高，就越不透明，也越不可靠。我们会被自己的宠物吸引，是因为宠物不会撒谎。

transcript.text: One of the first steps in dealing with emotions such as anger or fear is to acknowledge them as normal and human. There is nothing sinful or immoral about being emotional, unless your emotions make you inhuman, insensitive and cruel to others. Feelings of guilt associated with emotions are more devastating and damaging than the experience of emotion itself. So when you deal with the problem of emotions, you should learn not only how to control them but also how to accept them and manage the guilt and anguish arising from them.
transcript.zh: 处理愤怒或恐惧等情绪的第一步之一，是承认它们是正常的人类情感。情绪化本身没有任何罪恶或不道德之处，除非你的情绪使你变得不人道、麻木不仁并且残酷地对待他人。与情绪相关的内疚感，比情绪本身的体验更具破坏性，也更令人痛苦。因此，当你处理情绪问题时，不仅要学会如何控制情绪，还要学会如何接受情绪，并管理由此产生的内疚和苦恼。

transcript.text: Our brains are made up of a primitive inner core and a more evolved and rational outer core. Most of the time, the rational part of the mind controls the information coming from the primitive core and makes its own decisions as to what to do and how to respond. However, during critical situations, especially when a threat is perceived, the outer core loses control and fails to regulate the impulses and instinctual responses coming from the primitive brain. As a result, we let disturbing thoughts and emotions arise in our consciousness and surrender to our primitive behavior.
transcript.zh: 我们的大脑由一个原始的内部核心和一个进化程度更高、更具理性的外部核心组成。大多数时候，心智中理性的部分会控制来自原始核心的信息，并自行决定该做什么以及如何回应。然而，在关键情境下，尤其是在察觉到威胁时，外部核心会失去控制，无法调节来自原始大脑的冲动和本能反应。结果，我们让令人不安的思想和情绪进入意识，并屈从于原始的行为方式。

transcript.text: In times of emotional turmoil, remember that emotions arise because your senses are wired to the primitive part of your mind which is self-regulated, autonomous and spontaneous. Your rational mind does not always deal with the messages coming from it effectively. These messages are part of your survival mechanism and should not be stifled simply because emotions are unhealthy and betray your weaknesses. When emotions arise, instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver. This way you make use of your emotions without losing your balance and inner stability.
transcript.zh: 在情绪动荡时期，请记住，情绪之所以产生，是因为你的感官与心智中那个具有自我调节能力、自主性和自发性的原始部分相连。你的理性思维并不总能有效处理来自这一部分的信息。这些信息是你生存机制的一部分，不应仅仅因为情绪不健康、会暴露你的弱点，就被压抑。当情绪出现时，不要压抑它们，而要关注它们，并努力理解它们试图传达的信息。这样，你就能利用自己的情绪，同时不失去平衡和内在的稳定。

transcript.text: Good morning, class. My topic today is how to feed a hungry world. The world's population is expected to grow from 6.8 billion today to 9.1 billion by 2050. Meanwhile, the world's population more than doubled from 3 billion between 1961 and 2007. Simultaneously, food production has been constrained by a lack of scientific research. Still, the task of feeding the world's population in 2050 seems easily possible.
transcript.zh: 同学们，早上好。今天我要讲的主题是如何养活一个饥饿的世界。预计世界人口将从目前的68亿增长到2050年的91亿。与此同时，世界人口在1961年至2007年间从30亿增加了一倍多。与此同时，粮食生产又受到科学研究不足的限制。尽管如此，到2050年养活世界人口似乎仍然完全可行。

transcript.text: What is needed is a second green revolution. This is an approach that is described as the sustainable growth of global agriculture. Such a revolution will require a wholesale shift of priorities in agricultural research. There is an urgent need for new crop varieties. They must offer higher yields but use less water, nitrogen-rich fertilizers or other inputs. These new crops must also be more resistant to drought, heat and pests. Equally crucial is lower-tech research into basics such as crop rotation and mixed farming of animals and plants on small farms.
transcript.zh: 我们需要的是第二次绿色革命。这是一种被称为全球农业可持续增长的方式。这样的革命需要彻底改变农业研究的优先事项。人们迫切需要培育新的作物品种。这些品种必须提高产量，同时减少对水、富含氮的肥料或其他投入品的使用。这些新品种还必须更能抵抗干旱、高温和害虫。同样重要的是开展技术含量较低的研究，探讨作物轮作以及小农场中动植物混合养殖等基础问题。

transcript.text: Developing nations could score substantial gains in productivity by making better use of modern technologies and practices. But that requires money. It is estimated that to meet the 2050 challenge, investment must double to 83 billion US dollars a year. Most of that money needs to go towards improving agricultural infrastructure. Everything from production to storage and processing must improve. However, research agendas need to be focused on the needs of the poorest and most resource-limited countries. It is there that most of the world's population lives and it is there the population growth over the next decades will be the greatest.
transcript.zh: 发展中国家可以通过更好地利用现代技术和生产实践，大幅提高生产率。但这需要资金。据估计，为应对2050年的挑战，投资必须翻一番，达到每年830亿美元。其中大部分资金需要用于改善农业基础设施。从生产到储存和加工的各个环节都必须得到改进。然而，研究议程需要着眼于最贫困且资源最有限国家的需求。世界上大多数人口生活在那里，未来几十年人口增长最为迅速的地方也在那里。

transcript.text: To their credit, the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view. In March, for example, they came together at the first Global Conference on Agricultural Research to begin working out how to change research agendas to help meet the needs of farmers in poorer nations. But these plans will not bear fruit unless they get considerably more support from policy-makers.
transcript.zh: 值得肯定的是，世界各国的农业科学家正在采取这样广泛的视角。例如，今年3月，他们齐聚首届全球农业研究大会，开始研究如何改变研究议程，以帮助满足较贫困国家农民的需求。但是，除非得到政策制定者大力增加的支持，这些计划将不会结出成果。

transcript.text: The growth in public agricultural-research spending peaked in the 1970s and has been shrinking ever since. The big exception is China, where spending has far surpassed other countries over the past decade. China seems set to transition to become the key supplier of relevant science and technology to poorer countries. But developed countries have a humanitarian responsibility too. Calls by scientists for large increases in the appropriation of funds for public spending on agricultural research are more than justified.
transcript.zh: 公共农业研究支出的增长在20世纪70年代达到顶峰，此后一直在缩减。中国是一个明显的例外，过去十年中，中国的相关支出已经远远超过其他国家。中国似乎将转型为向较贫困国家提供相关科学技术的主要供应者。但发达国家同样负有提供人道主义援助的责任。科学家们呼吁大幅增加公共农业研究支出的拨款，这一要求完全合理。

Conversely, she says, opting for clothes that fit well and 26______ with your sense of style can improve your confidence.

passages.title: Section B 长篇阅读匹配

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A recent analysis found that most research mischaracterizes the relationship between music and skills enhancement.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: In 2004, a paper appeared in the journal Psychological Science, titled "Music Lessons Enhance IQ." The author, composer and psychologist Glenn Schellenberg had conducted an experiment with 144 children randomly assigned to four groups: one learned the keyboard for a year, one took singing lessons, one joined an acting class, and a control group had no extracurricular training. The IQ of the children in the two musical groups rose by an average of seven points in the course of a year; those in the other two groups gained an average of 4.3 points.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Schellenberg had long been skeptical of the science supporting claims that music education enhances children's abstract reasoning, math, or language skills. If children who play the piano are smarter, he says, it doesn't necessarily mean they are smarter because they play the piano. It could be that the youngsters who play the piano also happen to be more ambitious or better at focusing on a task. Correlation, after all, does not prove causation.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The 2004 paper was specifically designed to address those concerns. And as a passionate musician, Schellenberg was delighted when he turned up credible evidence that music has transfer effects on general intelligence. But nearly a decade later, in 2013, the Education Endowment Foundation funded a bigger study with more than 900 students. That study failed to confirm Schellenberg's findings, producing no evidence that music lessons improved math and literacy skills.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Schellenberg took that news in stride while continuing to cast a skeptical eye on the research in his field. Recently, he decided to formally investigate just how often his fellow researchers in psychology and neuroscience make what he believes are erroneous—or at least premature—causal connections between music and intelligence. His results, published in May, suggest that many of his peers do just that.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: For his recent study, Schellenberg asked two research assistants to look for correlational studies on the effects of music education. They found a total of 114 papers published since 2000. To assess whether the authors claimed any causation, researchers then looked for telltale verbs in each paper's title and abstract, verbs like "enhance," "promote," "facilitate," and "strengthen." The papers were categorized as neuroscience if the study employed a brain imaging method like magnetic resonance, or if the study appeared in a journal that had "brain," "neuroscience," or a related term in its title. Otherwise the papers were categorized as psychology. Schellenberg didn't tell his assistants what exactly he was trying to prove.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: After computing their assessments, Schellenberg concluded that the majority of the articles erroneously claimed that music training had a causal effect. The overselling, he also found, was more prevalent among neuroscience studies, three quarters of which mischaracterized a mere association between music training and skills enhancement as a cause-and-effect relationship. This may come as a surprise to some. Psychologists have been battling charges that they don't do "real" science for some time—in large part because many findings from classic experiments have proved unreproducible. Neuroscientists, on the other hand, armed with brain scans and EEGs(脑电图), have not been subject to the same degree of critique.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: To argue for a cause-and-effect relationship, scientists must attempt to explain why and how a connection could occur. When it comes to transfer effects of music, scientists frequently point to brain plasticity—the fact that the brain changes according to how we use it. When a child learns to play the violin, for example, several studies have shown that the brain region responsible for the fine motor skills of the left hand's fingers is likely to grow. And many experiments have shown that musical training improves certain hearing capabilities, like filtering voices from background noise or distinguishing the difference between the consonants(辅音) 'b' and 'g'.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: But Schellenberg remains highly critical of how the concept of plasticity has been applied in his field. "Plasticity has become an industry of its own," he wrote in his May paper. Practice does change the brain, he allows, but what is questionable is the assertion that these changes affect other brain regions, such as those responsible for spatial reasoning or math problems.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Neuropsychologist Lutz Jancke agrees. "Most of these studies don't allow for causal inferences," he said. For over two decades, Jancke has researched the effects of music lessons, and like Schellenberg, he believes that the only way to truly understand their effects is to run longitudinal studies. In such studies, researchers would need to follow groups of children with and without music lessons over a long period of time—even if the assignments are not completely random. Then they could compare outcomes for each group.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Some researchers are starting to do just that. The neuroscientist Peter Schneider from Heidelberg University in Germany, for example, has been following a group of children for ten years now. Some of them were handed musical instruments and given lessons through a school-based program in the Ruhr region of Germany called Jedem Kind ein Instrument, or "an instrument for every child," which was carried out with government funding. Among these children, Schneider has found that those who were enthusiastic about music and who practiced voluntarily showed improvements in hearing ability, as well as in more general competencies, such as the ability to concentrate.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: To establish whether effects such as improved concentration are caused by music participation itself, and not by investing time in an extracurricular activity of any kind, Assal Habibi, a psychology professor at the University of Southern California, is conducting a five-year longitudinal study with children from low-income communities in Los Angeles. The youngsters fall into three groups: those who take after-school music, those who do after-school sports, and those with no structured after-school program at all. After two years, Habibi and her colleagues reported seeing structural changes in the brains of the musically trained children, both locally and in the pathways connecting different parts of the brain.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: That may seem compelling, but Habibi's children were not selected randomly. Did the children who were drawn to music perhaps have something in them from the start that made them different but eluded the brain scanners? "As somebody who started taking piano lessons at the age of five and got up every morning at seven to practice, that experience changed me and made me part of who I am today," Schellenberg said. "The question is whether those kinds of experiences do so systematically across individuals and create exactly the same changes. And I think that is that huge leap of faith."

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: Did he have a hidden talent that others didn't have? Or more endurance than his peers? Music researchers tend, like Schellenberg, to be musicians themselves, and as he noted in his recent paper, "the idea of positive cognitive and neural side effects from music training (and other pleasurable activities) is inherently appealing." He also admits that if he had children of his own, he would encourage them to take music lessons and go to university. "I would think that it makes them better people, more critical, just wiser in general," he said.

paragraphs.label: O
paragraphs.text: But those convictions should be checked at the entrance to the lab, he added. Otherwise, the work becomes religion or faith. "You have to let go of your faith if you want to be a scientist."

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The trend toward rationality and enlightenment was endangered long before the advent of the World Wide Web. As Neil Postman noted in his 1985 book Amusing Ourselves to Death, the rise of television introduced not just a new medium but a new discourse: a gradual shift from a typographic(印刷的) culture to a photographic one, which in turn meant a shift from rationality to emotions, exposition to entertainment. In an image-centered and pleasure-driven world, Postman noted, there is no place for rational thinking, because you simply cannot think with images. It is text that enables us to "uncover lies, confusions and overgeneralizations, and to detect abuses of logic and common sense. It also means to weigh ideas, to compare and contrast assertions, to connect one generalization to another."

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The dominance of television was not confined to our living rooms. It overturned all of those habits of mind, fundamentally changing our experience of the world, affecting the conduct of politics, religion, business, and culture. It reduced many aspects of modern life to entertainment, sensationalism, and commerce. "Americans don't talk to each other, we entertain each other," Postman wrote. "They don't exchange ideas, they exchange images. They do not argue with propositions, they argue with good looks, celebrities and commercials."

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: At first, the web seemed to push against this trend. When it emerged towards the end of the 1980s as a purely text-based medium, it was seen as a tool to pursue knowledge, not pleasure. Reason and thought were most valued in this garden—all derived from the project of the Enlightenment. Universities around the world were among the first to connect to this new medium, which hosted discussion groups, informative personal or group blogs, electronic magazines, and academic mailing lists and forums. It was an intellectual project, not about commerce or control, created in a scientific research center in Switzerland. And for more than a decade, the web created an alternative space that threatened television's grip on society.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Social networks, though, have since colonized the web for television's values. From Facebook to Instagram, the medium refocuses our attention on videos and images, rewarding emotional appeals—'like' buttons—over rational ones. Instead of a quest for knowledge, it engages us in an endless zest(热情) for instant approval from an audience, for which we are constantly but unconsciously performing. (It's telling that, while Google began life as a PhD thesis, Facebook started as a tool to judge classmates, appearances.) It reduces our curiosity by showing us exactly what we already want and think, based on our profiles and preferences. The Enlightenment's motto(座右铭) of 'Dare to know' has become 'Dare not to care to know.'

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: According to a recent study, a small but growing proportion of the workforce is affected to some degree by a sense of entitlement. Work is less about what they can contribute but more about what they can take. It can lead to workplace dysfunction and diminish their own job satisfaction. I'm not referring to employees who are legitimately dissatisfied with their employment conditions due to, say, being denied fair pay or flexible work practices. I'm talking about those who consistently believe they deserve special treatment and generous rewards. It's an expectation that exists irrespective of their abilities or levels of performance.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: As a result of that discrepancy between the privileges they feel they're owed and their inflated sense of self-worth, they don't work as hard for their employer. They prefer instead to slack off. It's a tendency which many scholars believe begins in childhood due to parents who overindulge their kids. This thereby leads them to expect the same kind of spoilt treatment throughout their adult lives. And yet despite how these employees feel, it's obviously important for their manager to nonetheless find out how to keep them motivated. And, by virtue of that heightened motivation, to perform well.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The research team from several American universities surveyed more than 240 individuals. They sampled managers as well as team members. Employee entitlement was measured by statements such as "I honestly feel I'm just more deserving than others." The respondents had to rate the extent of their agreement. Employee engagement, meanwhile, was assessed with statements like "I really throw myself into my work." The findings revealed ethical leadership is precisely what alleviates the negative effects of employee entitlement. That's because rather than indulging employees or neglecting them, ethical leaders communicate very direct and clear expectations. They also hold employees accountable for their behaviors and are genuinely committed to doing the right thing. Additionally, these leaders are consistent in their standards. They're also less likely to deviate in how they treat employees.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: This means, when confronted by an entitled team member, an ethical leader is significantly disinclined to accommodate their demands. He or she will instead point out, constructively and tactfully, exactly how their inflated sense of deservingness is somewhat distorted. They'd then go further to explain the specific, and objective, criteria the employee must meet to receive their desired rewards. This shift away from unrealistic expectations is successful because entitled employees feel more confident that ethical leaders will deliver on their promises. This occurs because they're perceived to be fair and trustworthy.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The researchers, however, exercise caution by warning no one single response is the perfect remedy. But there's no denying ethical leadership is at least a critical step in the right direction.
